prompt: When an `{#if}` condition becomes false, what happens to the elements inside it?

choices.text: They stay on the page with `display: none` added by Svelte, ready to show again
choices.why: That is hiding; an `{#if}` takes them out of the page.

choices.text: They are destroyed
choices.why: Right, and created afresh when it becomes true again.

choices.text: They are kept in memory and reattached later
choices.why: Nothing is kept; a component inside starts afresh each time.

choices.text: They become disabled, so they can no longer be clicked
choices.why: Disabling is an attribute; the block removes the elements entirely.

prompt: Why must `{#if total === 0}` come before `{:else if doneMinutes === total}`?
hint: What are both values in an empty week?

choices.text: Svelte requires comparisons with zero to be the first branch of a chain
choices.why: There is no such rule; the order is the author's choice.

choices.text: In an empty week both are true, and the first true branch wins
choices.why: Right: 0 equals 0, so the order picks the sentence.

choices.text: `doneMinutes` is not ready until `total` has been checked
choices.why: Both are derived values, ready whenever read.

prompt: Match each week with the sentence the planner showed for it.

pairs.right: Every session this week is done.

prompt: When is a ternary in braces a better choice than an `{#if}` block?
hint: Values or pieces of the page?

choices.text: When the condition reads state, since blocks cannot react to state
choices.why: Blocks react to state; the planner's `{#if}` follows the week.

choices.text: When there are more than two cases to choose between
choices.why: More cases is exactly where `{:else if}` reads better.

choices.text: When it picks a word, such as `session` or `sessions`
choices.why: Right. A ternary chooses values; a block chooses markup.

choices.text: When the content should stay on the page and only be hidden from view while the condition is false
choices.why: That calls for `hidden` or CSS, not a ternary.

prompt: Match each form of `{#each}` with what it gives you.
With `{const day = addDays(week, i)}`, why did the days stay on 19 to 25 October after `Next week`?

choices.text: It ran once per `<li>`, and the seven `<li>` were not created again
choices.why: Right: a declaration in the markup behaves like one in the script.

choices.text: `addDays` caches its results and returned the old dates
choices.why: `addDays` is a plain function with no cache; it was simply not called again.

choices.text: The browser did not repaint the list until the page was reloaded
choices.why: The minutes beside them did change, so the list was updated.

choices.text: `week` cannot be read inside an `{#each}` block
choices.why: It can; the `$derived` version reads it there.

prompt: In the week of 19 October, how many minutes did the per-day list show for 20 Oct 2026?
How does the older `{@const day = addDays(week, i)}` differ from `{const day = addDays(week, i)}`?

choices.text: `{@const}` is computed once; `{const}` recalculates by itself
choices.why: The other way round.

choices.text: `{@const}` recalculates by itself; the new form needs `$derived`
choices.why: Right, and `{@const}` is now called legacy.

choices.text: They are two spellings of exactly the same thing, kept for compatibility
choices.why: The capture showed they behave differently when `week` changes.

prompt: A list of sessions can be sorted and have items deleted. Why is the index `i` a poor way to identify a session?

choices.text: Indexes start at 0, which confuses people reading the page
choices.why: Where it starts is not the issue; what it describes is.

choices.text: Svelte refuses to render an index for lists longer than seven items
choices.why: There is no such limit.

choices.text: It is a position, and after a change the same position holds another session
choices.why: Right. The days of a week are the safe case: they never move.

prompt: Without a key, a note was typed for the 19th and the list was sorted. Where did the note end up?

choices.text: In the field now labelled "Note for 24 Oct"
choices.why: Right: the first element kept its text and received the 24th's data.

choices.text: It moved with the 19th to the second row
choices.why: That is what the key made happen.

choices.text: It was lost, because sorting recreated both fields
choices.why: Nothing was recreated; the elements were reused.

choices.text: Svelte refused to sort a list with typed text in it
choices.why: It sorted; the transcript shows the new order.

prompt: What does `(session.id)` after the item change when the order of the list changes?

choices.text: Svelte sorts the list by id instead of the order given
choices.why: The order is still the derived list's; the key says who is who.

choices.text: Elements move with their items
choices.why: Right, so what an element holds goes with its session.

choices.text: Every element is destroyed and created again on each change
choices.why: That is `{#key}` on a whole block, not a key in a list.

choices.text: The id is shown to screen readers as the row's name
choices.why: A key is not rendered anywhere.

prompt: Match each key with what goes wrong with it, or right.

pairs.right: Same as no key: a position
Fails when the list is reloaded as new objects
Two sessions on one date collide
Identifies the session and never changes

prompt: In `{#each shown as session (session.id)}`, the part in brackets is called the ___.
Put the branches of `{#await}` in the order the page went through them on a successful load.
items: `Loading the planner…`, while the promise is pending
The promise resolves with the data
trap: The `{:then}` content needs the value, so it cannot come before the promise resolves.

prompt: The first version failed with `ssr_fetch_relative_url`. Why?
hint: The script also runs somewhere else.

choices.text: `/planner.json` did not exist, because `static` is not served in development
choices.why: It is served; the browser fetched it once the guard was added.

choices.text: On the server, a relative address has no page to be relative to
choices.why: Right: the server ran `load()` while rendering the HTML.

choices.text: `fetch` does not exist in Node 22
choices.why: Node 22 has `fetch`; the problem was the relative address.

choices.text: JSON files cannot be fetched, only imported
choices.why: The browser fetched it fine.

prompt: With the `browser` guard, what does the HTML sent by the server contain inside `<main>`?

choices.text: The whole planner, rendered from the data
choices.why: The server never had the data; lesson 13 changes that.

choices.text: An empty `<main>`, since nothing in the template is rendered on the server until JavaScript runs
choices.why: The heading and the pending branch were rendered.

choices.text: The heading and `Loading the planner…`
choices.why: Right: on the server the promise never settles.

choices.text: The error message from the `{:catch}` branch
choices.why: Nothing rejected on the server; the promise stays pending.

prompt: Why does `load()` check `response.ok` and throw, instead of calling `response.json()` straight away?

choices.text: `fetch` resolves on a 404, so without the check the error would be a JSON parse failure
choices.why: Right, and the check gives `{:catch}` a useful message.

choices.text: `fetch` retries forever on a 404 unless something throws
choices.why: `fetch` does not retry.

choices.text: `{#await}` ignores rejected promises unless an error is thrown
choices.why: A rejected promise reaches `{:catch}`; throwing is how it rejects.

prompt: Why does the error paragraph have `role="alert"`?

choices.text: It makes the text red
choices.why: A role says nothing about colour.

choices.text: A screen reader announces it as soon as it appears
choices.why: Right, instead of waiting for somebody to find it.

choices.text: It stops the page from loading any further
choices.why: It changes how the text is announced, nothing else.

choices.text: SvelteKit requires it on every `{:catch}` branch
choices.why: Nothing requires it; it is the right thing for an error.

prompt: What does `{#key week}…{/key}` do when `week` changes?

choices.text: Gives every element inside a key for list sorting
choices.why: That is a key in `{#each}`, a different thing.

choices.text: Destroys its content and creates it again
choices.why: Right, so the form starts with its initial values.

choices.text: Passes `week` to every component inside as a prop
choices.why: No prop is passed; `AddSession` knows nothing about weeks.

choices.text: Prevents the content from updating while `week` changes
choices.why: It does the opposite: it throws the content away and builds it again.

prompt: A component does not update when a prop changes, and someone wraps it in `{#key}` to force it. What is the real problem, most likely?

choices.text: Props never update without `{#key}`
choices.why: They do; `WeekTotal` followed its prop from lesson 3.

choices.text: The parent passed the prop with the wrong syntax, which Svelte reads as a constant
choices.why: Any `prop={value}` is reactive.

choices.text: It reads the prop once, or lacks a `$derived`
choices.why: Right. `{#key}` hides that bug by throwing the component away.

prompt: Match each tool with the job it does.
hint: Two keep things alive, one starts over.

pairs.right: Keeps each element with its item
Starts its content again on change
Keeps a value following the state

prompt: After wrapping `AddSession` in `{#key week}` and pressing `Next week`, the date field was ___.
Which of these does a `{#key}` block solve better than the alternatives? Choose all that apply.
hint: State belonging to one value of something outside.

choices.text: A form whose typed date belongs to one week
choices.why: Yes: the lesson's case.

choices.text: A transition that should play again each time a value changes
choices.why: Yes: lesson 9 uses it for this.

choices.text: A list whose notes must follow their sessions when sorted
choices.why: No: that is a key in `{#each}`.

choices.text: A label that should follow `week`
choices.why: No: that is `$derived`.

prompt: The planner should show `No courses yet` when the course list is empty. Which is the most direct way?

choices.text: An `{#await}` around the list
choices.why: Nothing is being waited for.

choices.text: A `{#key}` on the list's length
choices.why: That restarts content; it does not choose a message.

choices.text: An `{:else}` inside the `{#each}`
choices.why: Right: its content shows when the list is empty.
